O.content: The label "May" is attached below the rightmost dark-red bar.
The May bar is visibly much shorter than each of the Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, and Mar bars.
No printed critical threshold, escalation criterion, or routing legend is visible on the chart.

B.text: If low usage requires standard follow-up unless a stated critical threshold or escalation rule is met, then a visibly low May value alone supports standard low-usage follow-up rather than critical escalation.
B.conditions: The chart supplies no printed critical threshold, baseline, or routing rule; this interpretation assumes escalation cannot be inferred solely from relative bar height.

O.content: The label "May" is attached below the rightmost dark-red bar.
The May bar is visibly much shorter than each of the Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, and Mar bars.
The vertical axis is labeled "Grid energy use (kWh)" and its printed tick labels increase upward from 10,000 to 40,000.
A broken-axis mark is visible near the bottom of the y-axis.

B.text: If each bar is bound to its x-axis month label and bar height encodes grid-energy use on the upward y-axis, then May's much shorter bar represents lower use than every other displayed month; if the routing policy treats such an isolated, extreme low value as critical, select critical-anomaly review.
B.conditions: Assumes the truncated y-axis still preserves valid height ordering and that an extreme relative low value, without a displayed policy threshold, qualifies as critical.
